mcqs.q: A Class III semi-adjustable articulator is defined as an instrument that simulates condylar pathways by using:
opts: Averages or mechanical equivalents for all or part of the motion
A direct pantographic tracing of the patient's own condylar path
A fixed 30-degree inclination in every case
A single static registration taken in centric relation
mcqs.explain: It simulates condylar pathways by using averages or mechanical equivalents for all or part of the motion.

mcqs.q: Which capability does a Class III articulator have that a Class II articulator lacks?
opts: It allows for orientation of the casts relative to the joints
It allows vertical motion of the upper member
It can hold a wax set-up during tooth arrangement
mcqs.explain: Orientation of the casts relative to the joints — via a face-bow — is precisely what the Class II instrument cannot do.

mcqs.q: The term ARCON was derived by Bergstrom from which two words?
mcqs.explain: 'ARCON' was derived by Bergstrom from the words ARticulator CONdyle.

mcqs.q: In an ARCON articulator, the condylar analogs are located in the:
mcqs.explain: The arcon articulator maintains anatomic guidelines by condylar analogs in the mandibular element and fossae assemblies within the maxillary element.

mcqs.q: In an ARCON articulator, the fossae assemblies are located within the:
opts: Lower member, beside the incisal pin
mcqs.explain: The fossae assemblies — the equivalent of the glenoid fossa — belong to the maxillary (upper) element.

mcqs.q: On an ARCON instrument, the condylar element / analog / sphere is attached to the:
opts: Mounting ring of the upper cast
mcqs.explain: On an arcon articulator the condylar sphere is on the lower member — the anatomically correct arrangement.

mcqs.q: A NON-ARCON articulator is one whose condylar PATH components are part of the:
mcqs.explain: In a non-arcon articulator the condylar path components are part of the lower member and the condylar replica components are part of the upper member.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes the non-arcon articulator?
opts: It is the reverse of the temporomandibular joint
It duplicates the temporomandibular joint exactly
It has no condylar elements at all
It is adjustable in three planes
mcqs.explain: The non-arcon articulator is the reverse of the TMJ — condylar element above, guidance track below.

mcqs.q: Which articulator is given as an example of an ARCON instrument?
mcqs.explain: The Hanau University series is the stated arcon example; the Hanau-H series and Dentatus are non-arcon.

mcqs.q: Which pair are given as examples of NON-ARCON instruments?
opts: The Hanau-H series and the Dentatus
The Hanau University series and the Stuart
The Stuart and the Denar D4A
The Dentatus and the Denar D4A
mcqs.explain: The Hanau-H series and the Dentatus are the non-arcon examples given.

mcqs.q: A student sees 'Hanau' stamped on an articulator and concludes it must be arcon. Why is this unsafe?
opts: Hanau makes both — the University series is arcon and the H series is non-arcon
Hanau makes only fully adjustable instruments
The arcon distinction does not apply to Hanau instruments
mcqs.explain: The brand name alone does not settle it: the Hanau University series is arcon while the Hanau-H series is non-arcon.

mcqs.q: Semi-adjustable articulators reproduce the condyle's curved path as:
opts: A second curve of smaller radius
A series of three short arcs
mcqs.explain: The condyle travels a curved path in mandibular movements, and this is reproduced in semi-adjustable articulators as a straight path.

mcqs.q: The guidance that a semi-adjustable articulator is able to adjust directly is the:
opts: Bennett angle, from right and left records
mcqs.explain: Semi-adjustable articulators have adjustable horizontal condylar guides.

mcqs.q: Which record is used to mount the UPPER cast on a semi-adjustable articulator?
opts: The right and left relation records
mcqs.explain: The arbitrary face bow record mounts the upper cast.

mcqs.q: Which record is used to mount the LOWER cast?
mcqs.explain: The centric relation record mounts the lower cast against the already-mounted upper cast.

mcqs.q: The protrusive record is taken in order to adjust the articulator's:
opts: Horizontal guidance, to correspond with the patient's horizontal condylar path inclination
Lateral guidance, to correspond with the patient's Bennett angle
Incisal guidance, to correspond with the patient's overbite
Intercondylar distance, to correspond with the patient's face width
mcqs.explain: The protrusive record adjusts the horizontal guidance so that it matches the patient's horizontal condylar path inclination.

mcqs.q: Hanau's formula is written as:
mcqs.explain: Hanau's formula is L = H/8 + 12.

mcqs.q: In Hanau's formula, L and H stand respectively for:
opts: The lateral condylar inclination and the horizontal condylar inclination
The lingual cusp angle and the horizontal overlap
The lateral guidance and the hinge axis angle
The length of the condylar path and its height
mcqs.explain: L is the lateral condylar inclination and H is the horizontal condylar inclination.

mcqs.q: A patient's protrusive record gives a horizontal condylar inclination of 38°. Using Hanau's formula, the lateral condylar guidance should be set to approximately:
A patient's protrusive record gives a horizontal condylar inclination of 40°. Using Hanau's formula, the lateral condylar guidance is:
What does the use of Hanau's formula tell you about the lateral condylar guidance on a semi-adjustable articulator?
opts: It is calculated from the horizontal setting rather than recorded from the patient
It is recorded directly from the patient's right and left excursions
It is fixed by the manufacturer and cannot be altered
It is derived from the intercondylar distance
mcqs.explain: The lateral setting is calculated from the horizontal one rather than recorded separately — another approximation that makes the instrument only semi-adjustable.

mcqs.q: The intercondylar distance of a semi-adjustable articulator is:
opts: Adjustable from the patient's face-bow record
mcqs.explain: Semi-adjustable articulators have a fixed intercondylar distance of about 110 mm.

mcqs.q: Regarding the incisal guide table, the semi-adjustable articulator differs from the average-value instrument in that its table is:
opts: Set only by a kinematic record
mcqs.explain: Semi-adjustable articulators have an adjustable incisal guide table; the Class II instrument's incisal guidance is fixed.

mcqs.q: A fully adjustable articulator has a complex condylar mechanism adjustable in which planes?
mcqs.explain: It is adjustable in the horizontal, sagittal and frontal planes, to replicate three-dimensional mandibular movement.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT listed as a use of fully adjustable articulators?
mcqs.explain: The listed uses are complex fixed partial denture construction, treating TMJ problems and full mouth reconstruction.

mcqs.q: With respect to the arcon classification, fully adjustable articulators are:
opts: Neither, since they have no condylar analog
mcqs.explain: All fully adjustable articulators are arcon instruments.

mcqs.q: Which two instruments are given as examples of fully adjustable articulators?
opts: The Stuart and the Denar D4A
The Hanau University series and the Dentatus
The Hanau-H series and the Stuart
The Dentatus and the Denar D4A
mcqs.explain: The Stuart articulator and the Denar D4A articulator are the stated examples.

mcqs.q: Which type of face bow is used to mount the upper cast on a FULLY adjustable articulator?
mcqs.explain: The fully adjustable instrument takes a kinematic face bow record; the arbitrary bow belongs to the semi-adjustable instrument.

mcqs.q: The right and left relation records taken for a fully adjustable articulator are used to adjust the:
mcqs.explain: Right and left relation records adjust the Bennett angle.

mcqs.q: The intercondylar distance of a fully adjustable articulator is:
opts: Not a feature of this class
mcqs.explain: Fully adjustable articulators have an adjustable intercondylar distance, unlike the fixed 110 mm of the semi-adjustable instrument.

mcqs.q: Which feature is found on a fully adjustable articulator but NOT on a semi-adjustable one?
opts: Right and left relation records to set the Bennett angle
A protrusive record to set the horizontal guidance
A centric relation record to mount the lower cast
mcqs.explain: Records 1 to 3 are common to both classes; the right and left relation records and the adjustable intercondylar distance are new at Class IV.

mcqs.q: A face bow is defined as:
opts: A caliper-like device used to record the relationship of the maxilla to the temporomandibular joint
A caliper-like device used to record the relationship of the mandible to the maxilla
An instrument used to measure the intercondylar distance directly
A tracing device used to record the Gothic arch
mcqs.explain: The face bow is a caliper-like device used to record the relationship of the MAXILLA to the TMJ.

mcqs.q: Because the facebow records only the maxilla to the joint, it follows that:
opts: A separate centric relation record is needed to mount the lower cast
The lower cast cannot be mounted at all
The intercondylar distance is automatically transferred
mcqs.explain: The facebow has nothing to do with the mandible, so a centric relation record is required to position the lower cast.

mcqs.q: The classification of face bows divides them first into:
mcqs.explain: The first division is arbitrary versus kinematic; the arbitrary bow then subdivides into conventional and ear piece.

mcqs.q: The conventional and ear piece face bows are both sub-types of the:
mcqs.explain: Both the conventional and the ear piece bows are arbitrary face bows.

mcqs.q: Conventional and ear piece face bows are used with which articulators?
mcqs.explain: Conventional and ear piece face bows are used with semi-adjustable articulators; the kinematic bow goes with fully adjustable instruments.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes an EAR PIECE face bow from a CONVENTIONAL one?
opts: It locates itself from the external auditory meati rather than from points marked on the skin
It records the true hinge axis rather than an average point
It is used with fully adjustable articulators
mcqs.explain: The ear piece bow locates from the external auditory meati; both remain arbitrary bows used with semi-adjustable articulators.

mcqs.q: Which face bow locates the patient's TRUE hinge axis rather than an average point?
mcqs.explain: The kinematic face bow finds the true axis; arbitrary bows — conventional and ear piece — use an average point.

mcqs.q: The future of articulators is stated to lie in:
mcqs.explain: The lecture closes with 'FUTURE OF ARTICULATORS: VIRTUAL ARTICULATORS'.

mcqs.q: An instrument carries its condylar spheres on the lower member, its fossae assemblies on the upper, adjustable horizontal condylar guides, a fixed intercondylar distance and an adjustable incisal guide table. It is:
mcqs.explain: The condylar sphere on the lower member makes it arcon; the adjustable horizontal guides with a FIXED intercondylar distance make it semi-adjustable.

mcqs.q: Which single approximation is the reason a Class III instrument is called SEMI-adjustable rather than fully adjustable?
opts: The condyle's curved path is reproduced as a straight path
The upper cast is mounted by face bow rather than by hand
The incisal guide table is adjustable
The condylar analog is on the lower member
mcqs.explain: The condyle travels a curved path, reproduced on the semi-adjustable instrument as a straight path — that approximation is what the 'semi' refers to.

mcqs.q: Which statement about intercondylar distance across the classes is correct?
opts: 100 mm on the mean value, about 110 mm on the semi-adjustable, adjustable on the fully
Fixed at 100 mm on every class of articulator
Fixed at 38 degrees on the fully adjustable
mcqs.explain: The mean value articulator carries the 100 mm Bonwill side; the semi-adjustable is fixed at about 110 mm; the fully adjustable is adjustable.

saqs.q: Define the Class III semi-adjustable articulator and state the capability that separates it from a Class II instrument.
saqs.a: An instrument that SIMULATES CONDYLAR PATHWAYS BY USING AVERAGES OR MECHANICAL EQUIVALENTS for all or part of the motion. Unlike the Class II instrument, these ALLOW FOR ORIENTATION OF THE CASTS RELATIVE TO THE JOINTS — that is, they accept a face-bow transfer.

ans.text: An instrument that simulates condylar pathways by using averages or mechanical equivalents for all or part of the motion.

head: CLASS II
CLASS III — the separating capability
rows: does not orient the motion to the joints
allows orientation of the casts relative to the joints — that is, it accepts a face-bow transfer

saqs.q: From what words was the term ARCON derived, and by whom?
saqs.a: From ARTICULATOR + CONDYLE, derived by BERGSTROM.

saqs.q: Define the arcon articulator and state which element sits on which member.
saqs.a: An instrument that MAINTAINS ANATOMIC GUIDELINES by the use of CONDYLAR ANALOGS IN THE MANDIBULAR ELEMENT and FOSSAE ASSEMBLIES WITHIN THE MAXILLARY ELEMENT. So the CONDYLAR ELEMENT / ANALOG / SPHERE is on the LOWER member and the CONDYLAR GUIDANCE / FOSSAE ASSEMBLIES on the UPPER member. This is the anatomically correct arrangement — in the patient the condyle belongs to the mandible and the fossa to the skull. Example: the Hanau University series.

ans.text: An instrument that maintains anatomic guidelines by using condylar analogs in the mandibular element and fossae assemblies within the maxillary element.

head: Element
Member
rows: Condylar guidance / fossae assemblies (≈ the glenoid fossa)

ans.text: This is the anatomically correct arrangement — in the patient the condyle belongs to the mandible and the fossa to the skull. Example: the Hanau University series.

saqs.q: Define the non-arcon articulator and state which element sits on which member.
saqs.a: An articulator whose CONDYLAR PATH COMPONENTS ARE PART OF THE LOWER MEMBER and whose CONDYLAR REPLICA COMPONENTS ARE PART OF THE UPPER MEMBER. So the CONDYLAR ELEMENT / ANALOG / SPHERE is on the UPPER member and the CONDYLAR GUIDANCE / TRACK / FOSSAE ASSEMBLIES on the LOWER member. THIS ARTICULATOR IS THE REVERSE OF THE TMJ. Examples: the Hanau-H series and the Dentatus.

ans.text: An articulator whose condylar path components are part of the lower member and whose condylar replica components are part of the upper member.
This articulator is therefore the reverse of the TMJ. Examples: the Hanau-H series and the Dentatus.

saqs.q: Compare arcon and non-arcon articulators in a table.
saqs.a: CONDYLAR ELEMENT/SPHERE — arcon: LOWER member; non-arcon: UPPER member. CONDYLAR GUIDANCE/TRACK/FOSSAE — arcon: UPPER member; non-arcon: LOWER member. RELATION TO THE REAL TMJ — arcon: maintains ANATOMIC guidelines; non-arcon: is the REVERSE of the TMJ. EXAMPLES — arcon: Hanau University series; non-arcon: Hanau-H series, Dentatus. Semi-adjustable articulators may be either, while ALL fully adjustable articulators are arcon.

ans.text: Semi-adjustable articulators may be either, while all fully adjustable articulators are arcon.

saqs.q: What approximation gives the semi-adjustable articulator its name?
saqs.a: THE CONDYLE TRAVELS A CURVED PATH in mandibular movements; this is reproduced in semi-adjustable articulators AS A STRAIGHT PATH. The instrument is designed to be adjusted so its movements simulate the jaw movements of the patient, but replacing the curve with a straight line is the compromise that makes it only SEMI-adjustable.

ans.text: The instrument is designed to be adjusted so its movements simulate the jaw movements of the patient — but replacing the curve with a straight line is the compromise that makes it only semi-adjustable.

saqs.q: List the records a semi-adjustable articulator accepts, and state what each is for.
saqs.a: (1) FACE BOW (ARBITRARY) record — to mount the UPPER cast. (2) CENTRIC RELATION record — to mount the LOWER cast. (3) PROTRUSIVE record — to adjust the HORIZONTAL guidance, to correspond with the patient's horizontal condylar path inclination. (4) The LATERAL CONDYLAR GUIDANCE is then adjusted by HANAU'S FORMULA. In addition it has a FIXED intercondylar distance of about 110 mm and an ADJUSTABLE incisal guide table.

head: Record
What it is for
rows: to adjust the horizontal guidance, to correspond with the patient's horizontal condylar path inclination
the lateral condylar guidance is adjusted by Hanau's formula

list: A fixed intercondylar distance of about 110 mm

saqs.q: State Hanau's formula, define its terms, and work it for a horizontal inclination of 38°.
saqs.a: L = H/8 + 12, where L is the LATERAL CONDYLAR INCLINATION and H the HORIZONTAL CONDYLAR INCLINATION. For H = 38°: L = 38/8 + 12 = 4.75 + 12 = 16.75 ≈ 17°. The lateral condylar guidance is then set to 17° on the instrument by its thumbnut.

steps: L ≈ 17° — set on the instrument by its thumbnut

saqs.q: Why is the use of Hanau's formula itself a limitation of the semi-adjustable articulator?
saqs.a: Because the LATERAL setting is CALCULATED FROM the horizontal one rather than RECORDED from the patient. The instrument never measures the patient's own lateral condylar path, so the Bennett angle it reproduces is a derived estimate — one more approximation on top of replacing the curved condylar path with a straight one.

ans.text: Because the lateral setting is calculated from the horizontal one, rather than recorded from the patient. The instrument never measures the patient's own lateral condylar path, so the Bennett angle it reproduces is a derived estimate — one more approximation on top of replacing the curved condylar path with a straight one.

saqs.q: Describe the Class IV fully adjustable articulator.
saqs.a: It has a COMPLEX CONDYLAR MECHANISM, ADJUSTABLE IN THE HORIZONTAL, SAGITTAL AND FRONTAL PLANES, to REPLICATE THREE-DIMENSIONAL MOVEMENT. These instruments ALLOW ORIENTATION OF THE CASTS TO THE TMJs AND SIMULATION OF MANDIBULAR MOVEMENTS WITH A HIGH DEGREE OF ACCURACY. USES — complex fixed partial denture construction, treating TMJ problems, and full mouth reconstruction. ALL ARE ARCON INSTRUMENTS — e.g. the Stuart articulator and the Denar D4A.

rows: a complex condylar mechanism, adjustable in the horizontal, sagittal and frontal planes, to replicate three-dimensional movement
allows orientation of the casts to the temporomandibular joints and simulation of mandibular movements with a high degree of accuracy
ALL are arcon instruments — e.g. the Stuart articulator and the Denar D4A

saqs.q: List the records a fully adjustable articulator accepts and say which of them are new compared with a semi-adjustable instrument.
saqs.a: (1) FACE BOW record — a KINEMATIC face bow — to mount the upper cast. (2) CENTRIC RELATION record — to mount the lower cast. (3) PROTRUSIVE record — to adjust the horizontal guidance. (4) RIGHT AND LEFT RELATION RECORDS — to adjust the BENNETT ANGLE. (5) An ADJUSTABLE INTERCONDYLAR DISTANCE. NEW at Class IV are the right and left relation records and the adjustable intercondylar distance; record 1 also changes from an ARBITRARY to a KINEMATIC face bow.

saqs.q: Compare semi-adjustable and fully adjustable articulators.
saqs.a: CONDYLAR PATH — semi: the curved path reproduced as a STRAIGHT path; fully: a COMPLEX mechanism replicating THREE-DIMENSIONAL movement. PLANES — semi: adjustable HORIZONTAL condylar guides; fully: HORIZONTAL, SAGITTAL and FRONTAL. FACE BOW — semi: ARBITRARY; fully: KINEMATIC. LATERAL GUIDANCE — semi: CALCULATED by Hanau's formula; fully: RECORDED from right and left relation records. INTERCONDYLAR DISTANCE — semi: FIXED at about 110 mm; fully: ADJUSTABLE. ARCON — semi: may be arcon or non-arcon; fully: ALL are arcon.

head: SEMI-ADJUSTABLE
FULLY ADJUSTABLE
rows: the curved path reproduced as a STRAIGHT path
recorded from right and left relation records

saqs.q: Define the face bow and explain why a separate record is still needed to mount the lower cast.
saqs.a: A CALIPER-LIKE DEVICE used to RECORD THE RELATIONSHIP OF THE MAXILLA TO THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT. Because it relates only the MAXILLA to the JOINT and says nothing about the mandible, a CENTRIC RELATION RECORD is required to position the lower cast against the already-mounted upper cast.

ans.text: A caliper-like device used to record the relationship of the maxilla to the temporomandibular joint.
Because it relates only the maxilla to the joint and says nothing about the mandible, a centric relation record is required to position the lower cast against the already-mounted upper cast.

saqs.q: Give the classification of face bows and state which articulator each is used with.
saqs.a: FACE BOWS divide into ARBITRARY and KINEMATIC. The ARBITRARY bow subdivides into the CONVENTIONAL face bow and the EAR PIECE face bow, both used with SEMI-ADJUSTABLE articulators. The KINEMATIC face bow is used with FULLY ADJUSTABLE articulators.

head: Face bow
Subtypes
Used with
rows: the conventional face bow · the ear piece face bow

saqs.q: What does a face bow actually locate, and how do the arbitrary and kinematic bows differ in finding it?
saqs.a: It locates the HINGE AXIS — the imaginary line between the condyles about which the mandible rotates in the sagittal plane. An ARBITRARY face bow locates it at an AVERAGE point: from marked skin points on the conventional bow, or from the external auditory meati on the ear piece bow. A KINEMATIC face bow finds the patient's TRUE axis, by having them open and close while the stylus is moved until it rotates without translating.

ans.text: It locates the HINGE AXIS — the imaginary line between the condyles about which the mandible rotates in the sagittal plane.

head: ARBITRARY face bow
KINEMATIC face bow
rows: locates it at an AVERAGE point — from marked skin points on the conventional bow, or from the external auditory meati on the ear piece bow
finds the patient's TRUE axis — the patient opens and closes while the stylus is moved until it rotates without translating

saqs.q: What is said to be the future of articulators, and why is it attractive?
saqs.a: VIRTUAL ARTICULATORS. The casts, the mounting and the condylar settings all exist as digital data, so the movement can be simulated in software — without the mechanical approximations the metal instrument imposes, such as reproducing the curved condylar path as a straight line.

ans.text: Virtual articulators. The casts, the mounting and the condylar settings all exist as digital data, so the movement can be simulated in software — without the mechanical approximations the metal instrument imposes, such as reproducing the curved condylar path as a straight line.
